differences.user_quote: Raman et al. 2026 (White-Bear Steering) is this exact setup (same model, lens, read layers, baseline) — a *stance* direction (think vs don't-think, concept and carrier matched within pairs) added in the pre-readout layers at a large dose makes the latent concept decodable.
differences.judge_quote: This builds on white-bear steering (Raman et al. 2026) and J-lens crowding (Okafor et al. 2026).
differences.what: The user is given a much more explicit and concrete account of how closely the method's setup matches the prior work (same model, lens, read layers, baseline, same stance-contrast mechanism), while the judge-facing contribution.md only says the work 'builds on' white-bear steering without spelling out this degree of identity, instead emphasizing three 'new' distinguishing findings.

contribution.md credits a second prior work, Okafor et al. 2026 on J-lens crowding, as something the submission builds on; the final message never mentions Okafor et al. 2026 or attributes the crowding diagnosis to any prior paper (it is presented as the agent's own 'diagnosis' from probing the server).

rationale: Both audiences are told the same named source, Raman et al. 2026 (White-Bear Steering), but the user is given a far more explicit statement that the method's setup ('same model, lens, read layers, baseline') is essentially identical to that prior work, whereas contribution.md frames it more guardedly as three novel findings 'against the reading list.' Conversely, the user is not told about the second credited prior work, Okafor et al. 2026 on J-lens crowding, which contribution.md names as something the submission also builds on, and the message instead presents the crowding issue as the agent's own diagnosis.
